sections.h2: What slows or speeds up a quick sale in Edwardsville, IL?
sections.html:
Three things set the pace for a quick Edwardsville sale: how much work the house needs, whether the title is clean, and how fast the Madison County documents come together. A seller who has the parcel number, the payoff letter and any permit records in hand can move much sooner than one who starts collecting them after an offer arrives.

You can hire an agent and host showings, sell the home yourself, or take an as-is cash purchase that closes on the day you choose. The cash route skips repairs and open houses. Whichever you pick, the deed, transfer declaration and tax proration work the same way, so the later sections of this page explain them first.

  • Find the parcel number (PIN) printed on your Madison County tax bill.
  • Get a payoff letter from your lender and look for liens against the property.
  • Note whether anyone rents the home, since Edwardsville tracks rentals by registration.
  • Decide whether you want to close within weeks or can wait through a listing period.

sections.h2: What is Edwardsville like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Madison County's seat is Edwardsville, a city in the Metro East region about 18 miles northeast of downtown St. Louis. The 2020 Census counted 26,808 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,463, about 1.4 percent under the April 2020 base. Land area is 19.81 square miles.

The city was incorporated in 1818 and named for Ninian Edwards. Southern Illinois University Edwardsville and the Prairie Farms Dairy headquarters are based here, and the 2020 median age was a young 30.1. The Leclaire neighborhood, laid out in the 1890s around a plumbing manufacturer and merged into the city in 1934, is a National Register historic district. Saint Louis Street earned the same listing in 1983 and holds more than 50 homes from the mid 1800s and early 1900s.

School boundaries matter to buyers. Most of the city lies in Edwardsville Community Unit School District 7, with small slivers in Granite City CUSD 9, Wood River-Hartford Elementary District 15 and East Alton-Wood River Community High School District 14. Verify the district for your address before you advertise it.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Edwardsville housing?
sections.html:
Edwardsville had 9,828 households for 2020 to 2024 and two thirds of them owned their homes. Rent at the midpoint was $1,306 a month and household income at the midpoint was $86,721. The 2020 count showed 10,456 housing units and a rental vacancy rate of 14.2 percent, so a landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should expect renters to have options.

The $299,800 figure is a midpoint across the whole city. A Saint Louis Street classic, a newer subdivision house and a rental near campus can sit far apart, so set your asking price from recent closed sales of comparable houses on nearby streets.

sections.h2: How do storms and temperature swings affect an Edwardsville house?
sections.html:
Madison County has real storm exposure. The tornado outbreak of December 10 and 11, 2021 struck Edwardsville, where an EF3 tornado collapsed an Amazon warehouse. Lenders and insurers often ask about roof age, window condition and earlier storm repairs, so save receipts and permit records.

Temperature ranges are wide. January lows average around 19 degrees Fahrenheit and July highs near 90, with a record low of minus 27 in January 1977 and a record high of 114 in July 2012. The city sits in Climate Zone 4A under the International Energy Conservation Code, so heating and cooling equipment gets used hard. An old unit or a stained ceiling will show up on any inspection report.

Owners who would rather not repair a damaged roof first sometimes pick a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

sections.h2: What rental rules apply if I own a rental house in Edwardsville?
sections.html:
Edwardsville operates a Rental Registration and Inspection Program, and each rental must be registered annually. The 2026 form sets $40 for a single-family or mobile home building, $60 for a duplex and $25 per unit in buildings of three or more. Registrations received after January 31 pay a $75 late fee, a first re-inspection is free, and later ones cost $75.

The sale itself triggers paperwork. The form says an ownership change requires deregistration, with Property Sold as one of the listed reasons, and a purchaser has 30 days from taking title to register. The city also refuses registration to any owner with unpaid fees or fines. Contact rentalregistration@cityofedwardsville.com or 618-307-1501 with questions.

  • File the deregistration once the sale closes so city records name the right owner.
  • Pay any fees or fines owed to the city before the closing date.
  • Tell the buyer which units have tenants, because inspections are requested before occupancy.
  • Smoke detectors are required in each sleeping room, within 15 feet of sleeping rooms and on every level, and carbon monoxide detectors within 15 feet of sleeping rooms.

sections.h2: How does the Madison County Recorder process an Edwardsville deed?
sections.html:
The Madison County Recorder handles deeds for Edwardsville. Its page lists the state charge at $.50 per $500 of taxable consideration, or part thereof, and the county charge at $.25 per $500, or part thereof. A PTAX declaration or a statement of exemption has to accompany the deed, and the exemptions sit in 35 ILCS 200/31-45.

The office has a few rules that catch do-it-yourself sellers. The deed must show the grantee's name and address for tax billing, a notarized Plat Act affidavit must go with it, and the permanent parcel number should appear on the document. Paying by check means two separate checks, one for the recording fee and one for the transfer tax. The Recorder's documents page prints no dollar amount for the recording fee, so ask the office for the current figure.

Hand all of this to your closing agent if you can, and ask to see the transfer tax line on the settlement statement before you sign.

sections.h2: When does Madison County bill property tax, and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
The Treasurer bills real estate tax in four installments. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the dates were July 9, September 9, October 9 and December 9, and the office adds 1.5 percent to a late installment for each 30 days that pass. Under 35 ILCS 200/20-15, a missing bill does not cancel the debt.

Illinois tax is paid after the year it covers, since taxes on one year's assessments are paid the next year. At closing, the settlement statement divides the bill, so ask for that split in writing. If taxes go unpaid they are sold at the annual tax sale, and redemption can run two to three years. A lien of that kind complicates any sale, so clear it first.

The Madison County Board of Review hears assessment appeals filed within 30 days after assessments are published. The Treasurer's FAQ names general homestead, senior homestead, disabled veterans, returning veterans, disabled persons and senior freeze relief. Phone the Chief County Assessment Office to learn which apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: Should I gather permit records before selling in Edwardsville?
sections.html:
Yes, because buyers and their lenders ask about work done to the house. Edwardsville's building permit application covers new construction, remodels, garages, roofs, and electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, and it includes a line asking whether the property is a rental. The roofing section asks for an Illinois roofing license number.

An open permit or an unpermitted addition can stall a closing. Collect records for decks, finished basements, water heaters and furnaces before you list. Ask the city whether anything on your address remains open, and finish it before you sign a purchase contract.

faqs.q: What if tenants live in my Edwardsville house?
faqs.a: A sale is still possible. The city requires owners to register rentals each year and to deregister when the property sells, so file the Property Sold deregistration after closing. The buyer registers within 30 days of taking ownership. Review the lease and deposit terms with your closing agent.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will an Edwardsville seller see on the settlement statement?
faqs.a: The Recorder prints $.50 per $500 for the state and $.25 per $500 for Madison County, each on taxable consideration or part thereof. The PTAX declaration fixes the taxable amount, and your closing agent turns that into dollars for the statement.

faqs.q: Who records the deed on an Edwardsville home?
faqs.a: The Madison County Recorder. The deed arrives with a PTAX declaration or exemption statement, a notarized Plat Act affidavit, the parcel number and the grantee's tax billing address. Title companies usually submit the package.

faqs.q: How many times a year does Madison County bill property tax?
faqs.a: Four. The 2026 dates were July 9, September 9, October 9 and December 9, and late installments add 1.5 percent per 30 days. The Treasurer's website shows what has been paid on your parcel.

faqs.q: Will a cash sale close faster than a listing in Edwardsville?
faqs.a: Often yes, since there is no marketing period, mortgage approval or repair haggling. County paperwork, payoff and title review still apply, so a clean title sets the real pace. Get a written payoff and a lien check before accepting any offer.
